summary: - _“1) Approve the DOCO as claimed in the instant petition and condone the time over run._ - _3) Admit the capital cost as claimed in the Petition and approve the Additional Capitalization incurred/projected to be incurred._ - _4) Allow the petitioner to recover the shortfall or refund the excess Annual Fixed Charges, on account of Return on Equity due to a change in applicable Minimum Alternate/Corporate Income Tax rate as per the Income Tax Act, 1961 (as amended from time to time) of the respective financial year directly without making any application before the Commission as provided in Tariff Regulation 2019 as per para 8 above for respective block._ _and pass such other relief as the Commission deems fit and appropriate under the circumstances of the case and in the interest of justice.”_ 4. The Respondents are the distribution licensees and power departments that are procuring transmission service from the Petitioner, mainly the beneficiaries of the Western Region. 5. The Petitioner has served a copy of the Petition on the Respondents, and notice regarding the filing of this Petition has also been published in the newspapers in 6. The hearing in this matter was held on 25.2.2025, and the order was reserved. This order is issued considering the submissions made by the Petitioner in the Petition vide affidavit dated 14.2.2024 and subsequent affidavits dated 12.7.2024 and 24.2.2025, reply filed by MSEDCL vide affidavit dated 10.1.2025 and by MPPMCL vide affidavit dated 16.1.2025, and respective rejoinders filed by the Petitioner vide affidavits dated 21.2.2025. 7. Having heard the Petitioner’s representatives and after perusing the material on record, we proceed to dispose of the Petition. 28. MSEDCL has submitted that the alleged delay on account of COVID-19 is unjustified. MoP has given extension to projects that were already ongoing in March 2021, and the same is not applicable to the current project, as the project was approved by the CTUIL in June 2022. The general assertion made by the Petitioner regarding the shortage of semiconductors due to work-from-home conditions does not adequately justify the delay in procuring relay panels, as the production of these components was not significantly impacted by COVID-19. Further, the Petitioner had failed to substantiate its contentions with proper documents and details such as procurement orders, expected delivery timelines, follow-up correspondences for timely delivery, and has also not justified the same; rather, it has vaguely raised the same. There is no assertion as to the factum of events which hindered the project completion on account of Covid-19, and as such, the claim thereof in the absence of a material assertion with supporting documents, the claim of the Petitioner should not be permitted at the cost of the beneficiaries, including MSEDCL, and may not be allowed. MSEDCL has further submitted that it was the responsibility of the Transmission Service Provider (TSP) to plan the scheduling of civil works prior to the monsoon and to ensure the timely installation of equipment upon delivery. MSEDCL has also submitted that the lackadaisical approach of the Petitioner in planning has caused the said delay. Hence, the claim of the Petitioner under the present head cannot be allowed and thus deserves to be rejected at the threshold, particularly owing to the inefficiency in completing the project despite being well aware of the monsoon period in the interregnum, which is nothing but an inefficient planning of the project. 39. MPPMCL has submitted that the Petitioner has not substantiated by any documentary evidence about the rejection of the outage request by the WRLDC; thus, this contention is also not justified. 41. MSEDCL has submitted that the Petitioner has failed to substantiate its contention with proper documents and details such as procurement orders, expected delivery timelines, follow-up correspondences for timely delivery, and has also not justified the same, but has vaguely raised the same. Hence, the claim of the Petitioner cannot be allowed and may be rejected. respectively. Furthermore, the Petitioner has not submitted any specific documents to substantiate that the delay in the supply of the materials was due to the global shortage of semiconductor chips. There is also no contractual correspondence or record indicating any request or intimation of delay in the supply of materials due to such a shortage. 63. MPPMCL has countered that the Petitioner has failed to provide adequate documentation to support their claims, such as procurement orders, expected delivery timelines, follow-up correspondences, or weather department certifications. Without these documents, the reasons for delay remain unsubstantiated, and the COD should not be approved due to the insufficient justification. 64. MSEDCL has submitted that the lackadaisical approach of the Petitioner in planning has caused the said delay, and, hence, the claim of the Petitioner cannot be allowed. - _(d) Liabilities to meet award of arbitration or for compliance of the directions or order of any statutory authority or order or decree of any court of law;_ - _(a) Liabilities to meet award of arbitration or for compliance of the directions or order of any statutory authority, or order or decree of any court of law;_ 81. The Petitioner has also submitted the detailed liability flow statement as under: 101. The Petitioner has sought reimbursement of the fee paid by it for filing the instant Petition and the publication expenses. The Petitioner shall be entitled to the reimbursement of the filing fees and publication expenses in connection with the present Petition directly from the beneficiaries in accordance with Regulation 70(1) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations. 113. This order disposes of Petition No. 150/TT/2024 in terms of the above findings and discussions.
